1479. 1. April. Krumau. — Die Brüder Wok und Peter von Rosenberg über lassen dem Abte Thomas und dem Convente ihres Klosters in Hohenfurt für das von denselben abgetretene und zuт Dechterteiche gezogene Dorf Humno die beiden Dörfer Kuttau und Irsieglern. 1479. 11. December. Krumau. — Andreas, Propst von Kloster Schlägt, Johan nes, Pfarrer in Krumau, Wenzl von Sehwamberg, Konrad von Pelrowifz und Erasmus von Michnilz vidimiren die Urkunde, worin Kaiser Karl IV. dem Stifte zu Hohenfurt Steuerfreiheit bewilligt. 1480. 16. Juli. Mtthlhansen. — Abt Nikolaus und der Convent der Prämonstra- tenser zu Mählhausen treten mit dem Abte Thomas und dem Convente zu Hohen- furt in Confraternität.

CCLXVI. My Wok a Petr wlastnij bratrzij z Roznberka etc. gmenem nassim a ginych bratrzij y diediczuow nassichwyznawametiemto listem wssem wuobecz a predewssemi, ktoz geig vzrzie a czisti nebo cztucze slysseti budu, jakozgsme vdielali na panstwij nassem v Dechtarz rybnijk nowy weliky, kterymzto rybnikemzatopili a swedli gsme wes Humno a platu rocznieho piet kop a piet grossuownalidech tu osedlych, kterazto wes a plath prislussel gest welebnemu a nahoznemu v boze otczi a kniezi kniezi Thomano wi opathowi y con wentu klasstera nasseho vWissibrodie. Y prosili sme swrchupsaneho knieze opatha y bratrzij tehoz conwentu, ze gsu k tomu swolili a nam swu dobru wuoli w tom pro nasse dobre okazali, ze gsu od nas odmienu slussnu zase przigeli totizto wes Chudiegiow a wes Girziczkow s platy y os'py na panstwij nassem Roznberskym na lidech tu osedlych dole psanych, totizto we wsy w Chudiegiowie platu rocznieho Waczlaw puol cztrnadezta grosse a dwa czhery owsa, Janek puol cztrnadezta grosse a dwa czbery owsa, JanekRuozek puol cztrnadezta grosse a dwa czbery owsa, Matieg Rabat puol cztrnadezta grosse a dwa czbery owsa, a Beda sedmmez- czietma grossuow a cztirzi czbery owsa; a przi swatem Girzij schazij na swrchupsanych lidech za owes dwanadczt grossuow. A we wsy Girziczkowie plathu rocznieho: Gira se dworu geden funth peniez a cztirzi czbery owsa a trzi slepicze, Gira Michaluow syn dwanadczt 335 grossuow, dwa czbery owsa a dwie slepiczy, a Petr se cztwrti sedm grossuow a geden czber owsa, kterezto wsy swrchupsane Chudiegiow a Girziczkow s platy s ospy y s kury swrchupsanymi y s lidmi plat- nymi, s diedinami ornymi y neornymi, s lukami, s chrastmi s chra- stinami, s pastwami y s pastwisstiemi, s obczemi, s mezemi, s hra- niczem, iakozto od starndawna w swym polozenij zalezie y se wssy zwolij a wsselikym przislussenstwym, czoz k tiem wsem a lidem przislussie, tak se wssim, yakoz sme sam drzeli niez owssem sobie tu na tom ¡mi swym diediczom a buduczim prawa zadneho nepozuosta- wugicz, ani ktereho zwlasstenstwie, ku prawemu diediczslwij a plnemu panstwij postupili sme, a moczij listu tohoto postupugem swrchupsanemu kniezy opathowi klasstera Wyssebrodskeho nyniei- ssiemu y buducziemu y conwentu tehoz klasstera nynieyssiemu y buducziemu. A mame, dluzni sme a powinni slibugicze tiemto listem nassym, dobru nassi wieru krzestiansku nadepsanemu kniezy opa thowi y conwentu klasstera swrchupsaneho nynieissiemu y budu cziemu ty swrchupsane wsy se wssim gich przislussenstwim, czoz k tiem wsem przislussie, tak iakoz se swrchupisse a gmenuge, kdyz koliwiek od nidi my aneb nassi diediczi a buducij napomenuti budem, hned nit prwnie suchedni, neb na druhe bezelsti, a konecznie na trzetij suchedni wedczky zemske a w acta wloziti a zapsati ku pra wemu gich diedicztwij a plnemu panstwij a zprawcze hodne posta- witi wedle rzadu a obyczege zemie Czeske czistie bez zmatku wsse- likterakeho tak, iakoz zemie Czeska za prawo ma, tak aby swrchup sane wsy s platy, s ospy, s kury y s lidmi swrchupsanymi k tomu boziemu domu a klasstera swrchupsanemu wiecznie przislusseti, drzany a poziwani byli bez nassie a nassich diediczuow y buduczich wsselikterake przekazky. Tomu na potwrzcnie peczeti nasse wlastnie rozkazali sme prziwiesiti k tomuto listu dobrowolnie, genz gest dan a psan na Crumlowie lethu od narozenie syna bozieho tisiczieho cztirzsteho sedmdesateho dewateho ten cztwrtek przed kwietnu nedielij. Zwei, an Pergamentstreifen hängende Siegel in rothem Wachs. a) Ziem lich gross. Ein Schild, worauf eine Rose, wird von einem rosengezierten Helm überdeckt. — Sigilu . Woccouis . De . Rosenberg. b) Klein; Schild mit einer Rose. — SXPetri X De X Rosenberg X — Die Pergamentstreif en sind mit den Namen der Siegler bezeichnet. 336 CCLXVIL 1479. 11. December. Quia mediante caritate, que vinculum perfecciouis ab apostolo predicatur, membra singula in corpore sanete matris ecclesie sibi in vicem coniunguntur et Christo suo capiti ad percipiendum per ipsum et in ipso graciarum spiritualium influenciam vniuntur, tanto liber'ius atque libencius sinum caritatis in ampliando confraternitatis consorcium dilatamus, quanto ad participacionem fructus huiusmodi feruencius anhelamus. Vestrarum igitur caritatum affectu et religiositate moti matura deliberaeione prehabita plene confraternitatis bonorum scilicet omnium consorcium et communionem in missis oracionibus elemosinis abstinenciis et vigiliis ac aliis virtu- tum exerciis, que diuina clemencia per presentes nos et successores nostros in dicto nostro monasterio Milocensi dignabitur operari, vobis ae successoribus vestris fraternilatem concedimus et presencium tenore roboramus, adicientes quod cum obitus vuius uel plurium predicti monasterii uestri professi uel professorum nobis nuncciatus fuerit, missam defunctorum cum exsequiis iuxta conswetudinen nostri monasterii persoluemus, sed et singuli sacerdotes missas legentes singulas missas, clerici ver-o missas non legentes officium defunc torum totum vesperas scilicet vigilias nouem leccionum cum laudibus, conuersi autem centum „pater noster" cum totidem „aue Maria" in remedium animarum eorumdem dicent. entries.english:
1479, 1 April, Krumau. The brothers Wok and Peter von Rosenberg transfer to Abbot Thomas and the convent of their monastery at Hohenfurt the villages of Kuttau and Irsieglern in their Rosenberg lordship, with their rents and dues, in exchange for the village of Humno, which the monastery had surrendered and which the brothers had flooded to create the Dechtar fishpond.

CCLXVI. We, Wok and Peter, full brothers of Rosenberg, in our own name and that of our other brothers and heirs, make known to all who see or read this letter, or hear it read, that we have built a large new fishpond on our lordship at Dechtar. By means of this pond we flooded and displaced the village of Humno, whose inhabitants owed an annual rent of five kopas and five groschen and which belonged to the venerable and devout father in God, Lord Thomas, abbot, and the convent of our monastery at Hohenfurt. We asked the said lord abbot and the brothers of his convent, and they consented and showed us their goodwill for our benefit, accepting from us a fair compensation: the villages of Chudějov and Jiřičkov, with their rents and dues, in our Rosenberg lordship, including the tenants named below.

In Chudějov the annual rent is: Václav, fourteen and a half groschen and two korce of oats; Janek, fourteen and a half groschen and two korce of oats; Janek Ruozek, fourteen and a half groschen and two korce of oats; Matěj Rabat, fourteen and a half groschen and two korce of oats; and Beda, seventeen groschen and four korce of oats. At Saint George's feast the above-mentioned tenants also owe twelve groschen in oats. In Jiřičkov the annual dues are: Jiří of the manor, one pound of money, four korce of oats, and three hens; Jiří, son of Michal, twelve groschen, two korce of oats, and two hens; and Petr the fourth, seven groschen and one korec of oats.

We have transferred and by this letter transfer the said villages of Chudějov and Jiřičkov, with the specified rents, oats, hens, and rent-paying people, their arable and uncultivated lands, meadows, scrubland and woodland, pastures and grazing grounds, commons, boundaries and limits, as they have existed from of old in their proper situation, together with all their rights and appurtenances belonging to those villages and people. We transfer them just as we ourselves have held them, without retaining for ourselves or our heirs any right or special claim, into the true inheritance and full lordship of the said present and future lord abbot of the Hohenfurt monastery and its present and future convent.

By this letter we promise and are bound, on our good Christian faith, to the said present and future abbot and convent that, whenever we or our heirs and successors are summoned concerning those villages and their appurtenances as described above, we shall promptly appear before the provincial court: at the first summons on the first court day, or at the second on the second court day, and finally at the third on the third court day, and have the villages entered and recorded in the land registers as their true inheritance and full lordship, properly established according to the law and custom of the Kingdom of Bohemia, plainly and without any confusion, as Bohemian law requires. Thus the said villages, with their rents, oats, hens, and named people, shall belong forever to the said religious house and monastery, and be held and enjoyed without any hindrance by us, our heirs, or our successors. In confirmation, we have willingly ordered our own seals to be attached to this letter. Given and written at Krumau in the year of the birth of the Son of God 1479, on the Thursday before Easter.

Two seals in red wax hang from parchment strips. (a) Rather large: a shield bearing a rose, surmounted by a rose-decorated helmet; legend: “Seal of Wok of Rosenberg.” (b) Small: a shield with a rose; legend: “Seal of Peter of Rosenberg.” The parchment strips bear the names of the sealers.

CCLXVII. 11 December 1479, Krumau. Andreas, provost of the monastery of Schlägl; Johannes, parish priest at Krumau; Wenzl von Schwamberg; Konrad von Petrowitz; and Erasmus von Michnitz authenticate the charter in which Emperor Charles IV granted the monastery at Hohenfurt exemption from taxes.

We, Andreas, by divine mercy provost of the monastery of the Blessed Virgin Mary at Plaga of the Premonstratensian Order; Johannes de Hericz, dean of Dudlehen, archdeacon of Bechin, and parish priest at Krumau; Wenceslaus von Schwamberg; Conrad von Petrowitz; and Erasmus von Michnitz, publicly acknowledge and declare by this present instrument that the reverend father in Christ, Lord Thomas, abbot of the monastery of the Most Blessed Virgin Mary at Altovad, of the Cistercian Order, situated at Krumau, presented and showed us a letter of the late most invincible and serene prince and lord, Lord Charles, of divine memory, most glorious King of the Romans and Bohemia, secured with his Majesty's hanging seal. It concerned certain liberties for the monastery at Altovad, namely exemption from royal taxes, individual taxes, levies, imposed contributions, compulsory services, extraordinary services, demands, lodging charges, subsidies, burdens, and any other obligations. We carefully examined this letter and found it sound and complete in every respect, neither erased nor cancelled, not suspect in any part, and altogether free from defect or suspicion. Its text follows word for word: “[The charter numbered XC follows.]”

We, the above-named Andreas, provost; Johannes, dean; Wenceslaus von Schwamberg; Conrad von Petrowitz; and Erasmus von Michnitz, having seen, read, heard, and carefully examined the aforesaid letter, clearly transcribed word for word, have made this present instrument at the request of the aforementioned lord abbot, not by mistake or carelessness, but deliberately and with the certain knowledge of us all. In witness and confirmation of all this, we have ordered our own seals to be attached to this instrument. Given at Krumau in the year of the Lord 1479, on the Saturday before Saint Lucy's feast day.

The charter is damaged; the text in square brackets is supplied from more recent copies. Four small seals (one described as a “guldengross”) hang from parchment strips; b and [the seal designated] 337 [?] are in red wax, d and e in black wax. (a) The seal of the provost of Schlägl is missing. (b) Damaged: the seal of Johannes, parish priest of Höritz, described previously. (c) A shield bearing a swan; legend: “Waczlaw von Swamberc.” (d) A shield divided vertically into two fields, the right field with three horizontal bars; above it a helmet with a half-wing; legend: “Kvnrat von Petrovic.” (e) The seal of Erasmus von Michnitz, known from another description.

CCLXVIII. 16 July 1480, Mühlhausen. Abbot Nikolaus and the convent of the Premonstratensians at Mühlhausen enter into confraternity with Abbot Thomas and the convent at Hohenfurt.

To the venerable and religious fathers and brothers in Christ, Lord Thomas, abbot, Jacob, prior, and the whole convent of the monastery of Altovad of the Cistercian Order in the diocese of Prague: we, the brothers Nikolaus, abbot, and Wenceslaus, prior, of the Premonstratensian Order in the same diocese, and the whole convent, send lasting greetings in the Lord with sincere affection of charity.

Since charity, which the Apostle calls the bond of perfection, joins each member to the others in the body of Holy Mother Church and unites them to Christ, its head, to receive through him and in him an outpouring of spiritual graces, we widen charity's embrace more freely and gladly by enlarging the fellowship of confraternity, the more fervently we desire to share in its fruits. Therefore, moved by affection for your charity and religious life, and after mature deliberation, we grant and confirm by this instrument to you and your successors the full fellowship and communion of all good works: masses, prayers, alms, fasts, vigils, and other virtuous observances which divine clemency will deign to bring about through us and our successors at our said monastery of Mühlhausen. We further provide that, when we are informed of the death of one or more professed members of your monastery, we shall celebrate a mass for the dead with the customary rites of our monastery. Each priest who celebrates mass shall say one mass; clerics who do not celebrate mass shall recite the entire office for the dead, namely vespers, the nine lessons of the vigil, and lauds; and the lay brothers shall say one hundred “Our Fathers” and as many “Hail Marys” for the repose of their souls. As witness and confirmation of all this, we have resolved to hand this instrument, sealed with our seals, to our aforesaid brothers. Given and executed at our monastery of Mühlhausen on the Sunday after the feast of Saint Margaret the Virgin, in the year of the Lord 1480.

Two seals hang from parchment strips. (a) Large, in black wax: an abbot with staff and book in a Gothic chapel, at his feet a shield bearing what may be the bust of Saint Norbert; legend: “Seal of Nikolaus, Abbot of the Monastery of Mühlhausen.” (b) Fairly large, in white wax: an abbot seated on a bench with book and staff, with an S on the right and an E on the left; legend: “Seal of the Convent of the Monastery of Mühlhausen.”
